Entry.EnglishText: Hand over 10 Aqua Spirit Gems?

Entry.JapaneseText: 道具屋 天地無用
Entry.EnglishText: Item Shop - The Rightside Up

Entry.JapaneseText: ヴァルハラ村
Entry.EnglishText: Valhalla Village

Entry.JapaneseText: 見つけてくれて サンキュー！
Entry.EnglishText: Oh, you found me! Thank you~!

Entry.JapaneseText: ご褒美よ！
Entry.EnglishText: Here, a reward!

Entry.JapaneseText: ……では、サラバっ！！
Entry.EnglishText: ...And with that... Farewell!

Entry.JapaneseText: おかげさまで、 採掘の人手は足りてるよ
Entry.EnglishText: Thanks to your help before, we've got plenty of people for now.

Entry.JapaneseText: 前みたいにおまえらの 手を借りるほどでもない
Entry.EnglishText: We're not so short-handed as to need your help again.

Entry.JapaneseText: お願い、ティアの花を……
Entry.EnglishText: Please, a Tear's Flower...

Entry.JapaneseText: ティアの花は、 <Red>ローンヴァレイ<White>の 奥の方にあるわ……
Entry.EnglishText: You can find Tear's Flowers growing deep in <Red>Lone Valley<White>...

Entry.JapaneseText: ……ティアの花……！ ………… ありがとう……
Entry.EnglishText: ...That's a Tear's Flower...! ...Thank you...

Entry.JapaneseText: なつかしい、この花…… 私の思い出の花……
Entry.EnglishText: It's nostalgic, this flower... It's full of memories...

Entry.JapaneseText: おねがい…… ぜひ、母にも見せてあげて
Entry.EnglishText: Please... You have to show it to my mother, too.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私の家は、村の東側、 川沿いに面した建物よ
Entry.EnglishText: Our home is a building on the east side of the village, facing the riverbank.

Entry.JapaneseText: メモリーさんかい？ あの人なら村を出てったよ
Entry.EnglishText: Are you looking for Memorie? If so, she's left the village.

Entry.JapaneseText: お母さんも重い病気なのに、 本人も病気だなんて、 気の毒すぎるわ……
Entry.EnglishText: Her mother's already terribly ill, and then come to find she's ill, herself... It's far too cruel...

Entry.JapaneseText: 自分が病気だって知られると、 お母さんが自分に気を使うから 村を離れることにしたって
Entry.EnglishText: When she learned of her own illness, she knew it would cause her mother to worry for her, so she went far away.

Entry.JapaneseText: 悲しいね
Entry.EnglishText: It's sad, isn't it?

Entry.JapaneseText: やぁ、君たち、 水精石は集まったかい？
Entry.EnglishText: Hey, it's you all. Did you gather those Aqua Spirit Gems?

Entry.JapaneseText: ああ、ありがと。 いただくよ
Entry.EnglishText: Ahh, thanks. Then, I'll take these.

Entry.JapaneseText: 先生も喜ぶよ、きっと。 また先生が戻ってきたら、 来てね
Entry.EnglishText: I'm sure the professor will be happy, too. Once he's returned, do swing by.

Entry.JapaneseText: 先生も君たちに とても会いたがってたから
Entry.EnglishText: He was really hoping to see you again, too.

Entry.JapaneseText: まぁ、そうだね
Entry.EnglishText: Well, that's alright.

Entry.JapaneseText: 先生が戻ってきてから 持ってきてくれたほうが いいかもね
Entry.EnglishText: It might be nicer if you handed them over yourself, once the professor's returned.

Entry.JapaneseText: ……なんだ、 まだ集まってないんだね
Entry.EnglishText: ...What, you don't have them yet?

Entry.JapaneseText: それじゃあ、 もし、集まったら、 持ってきてくれるかな
Entry.EnglishText: Well, then. If you do come across some, would you bring them here?

Entry.JapaneseText: あ、無理に、とは言わないから。 できれば、でいいからね
Entry.EnglishText: Ah, but you don't need to force yourselves. Only if you're able to.

Entry.JapaneseText: おなかすいた…… でも、泣かないよ
Entry.EnglishText: I'm very hungry... But, I won't cry.

Entry.JapaneseText: 泣いたら、 もっとおなか空くもん
Entry.EnglishText: 'Cause if I cry, I'll get even hungrier.

Entry.JapaneseText: ぼくかなしくても、なかないよ、 だって、お腹空くもん
Entry.EnglishText: Even if I'm sad, I won't cry. 'Cause I'm too hungry.

Entry.JapaneseText: それでも…… なみだ出ることって ある、よね？
Entry.EnglishText: But you know... Some tears do come out on their own, sometimes.

Entry.JapaneseText: きょうのごはん、 ちゃんとあるかな～
Entry.EnglishText: I wonder if I'll get to have any food today~

Entry.JapaneseText: 今日はなんだろ。 タマゴが食べられたら サイコーだな
Entry.EnglishText: What'll it be? It'd be suuuper nice if I could eat an egg.

Entry.JapaneseText: きのうは何も食べられ なかったから、きょうはたぶん、 ごはんの日なんだ
Entry.EnglishText: I didn't get anything to eat yesterday, so today's probably a meal day.

Entry.JapaneseText: あ……でも ３日にいっぺんって時も あるからわかんないかな……
Entry.EnglishText: Ah...but... Sometimes three days pass and I only get one meal... So, I dunno...

Entry.JapaneseText: おなか空いたよ～…… でもガマンするんだ
Entry.EnglishText: I'm very, very hungry~... But I'll in-dure it.

Entry.JapaneseText: ガマンしたら あしたはたんと ごちそうが食えるんだ
Entry.EnglishText: If I in-dure, then I'll get to eat a whoooole lot, tomorrow.

Entry.JapaneseText: きょうのごはんガマンしたら そのぶん、あした 倍の量食えるんだよ
Entry.EnglishText: If I in-dure not eating today, I'll get to eat twice as much tomorrow.

Entry.JapaneseText: おなかすいたら ごはんもおいしくなるしね
Entry.EnglishText: And when I'm hungry, food tastes even better.

Entry.JapaneseText: こんなとこで何してんだ、オラ！ ゆっくりしてくんだよ！
Entry.EnglishText: The hell are you doin' here, huh!? You enjoyin' yourself!? Relaxin'!?

Entry.JapaneseText: 茶も飲んでくといいさっ！
Entry.EnglishText: Come 'n have some tea, too, why don'tcha!

Entry.JapaneseText: こんな村に何しに来やがった！ ま、ゆっくりしてけ！
Entry.EnglishText: What the hell'd you come to this village for!? Well, whatever! Relax! Enjoy your stay!

Entry.JapaneseText: ……別に怒ってるわけじゃねーぞ！ 声が大きいだけだ！
Entry.EnglishText: ...Nah, I'm not angry, or nothin'! This is just how I talk!

Entry.JapaneseText: 今日も明日も 食うもんがねーときた！
Entry.EnglishText: Nothin' to eat today! Nothin' to eat yesterday! So it's come to this, huh!

Entry.JapaneseText: しょうがねーな！ タワシでも食っとくかぁ！
Entry.EnglishText: Well, it is what it is! Guess I'll just eat a sponge, or somethin'!

Entry.JapaneseText: 大きい声出しとけば、 腹が空いたのも まぎれるってもんよ！
Entry.EnglishText: If ya shout loud enough, you'll forget all about how hungry you are!

Entry.JapaneseText: てめぇもやってみな！ 腹から声ぇ出しやがれ！
Entry.EnglishText: You try it out, too! C'mon, spit it out! Right from the chest! Nice and loud!

Entry.JapaneseText: 食うもんも水もねぇ！ こりゃ、オレら ひからびて死ぬな！
Entry.EnglishText: Nothin' to eat, and not a drop of water! At this rate, we're gonna shrivel up and die!

Entry.JapaneseText: なんてこたぁねぇっ！ 死ぬだけだろーがよ！
Entry.EnglishText: Well, who gives a damn! It's just dyin', so I'll just die!

Entry.JapaneseText: 覚悟はできてるさっ！ 明日、もう食うもんが なくなることくらいなっ！
Entry.EnglishText: I'm ready for it! Not a damn thing to eat tomorrow? Well, that suits me fine!

Entry.JapaneseText: ふん！
Entry.EnglishText: Humph!

Entry.JapaneseText: なんだろうね、長年夫婦ってのを やってると互いに素直に なれなくなっちまう！
Entry.EnglishText: We've been together all these years, but we just get more ornery the longer we're together! What's that about!?

Entry.JapaneseText: 決して、相手が嫌いに なったわけでもないのにね！
Entry.EnglishText: And you rest assured, we still like each other well enough! There's no problem there!

Entry.JapaneseText: 毎日毎日、大声を張り上げて ののしり合ってたら、 かえって腹が減るのに
Entry.EnglishText: Day after day, we scream and shout and curse at each other, and we just get hungrier and hungrier.

Entry.JapaneseText: バカな夫婦よね、 私たち
Entry.EnglishText: We're a couple of old fools, aren't we?

Entry.JapaneseText: あの人ったら、昨日から 何も食べてないのよ！
Entry.EnglishText: My husband's not eaten a thing since yesterday!

Entry.JapaneseText: そのくせに残ったパンを 全部、私にくれて…… バカじゃないの……！？
Entry.EnglishText: And yet he left me all the bread we've got left... Just what kind of fool is he!?

Entry.JapaneseText: 明日にはきっとちゃんと 食糧を仕入れてきてあの人にも 腹いっぱい食べさせるの！
Entry.EnglishText: Tomorrow, make no mistake, I'm going to top up our stocks of bread and rice, and *make* him fill his stomach!

Entry.JapaneseText: もう私ばかりが 食べさせられるなんて、 そんなことさせない！
Entry.EnglishText: I'm finished letting him force all our food on me! I'm just done with it!

Entry.JapaneseText: もう何日も 何も食べていないわ……！
Entry.EnglishText: It's been days and days since we last ate!

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、もういいわね、 あの人と一緒に死ねるなら、 それでいいって気がしてきた……
Entry.EnglishText: But that's fine enough. If I can die together with my husband, I'm happy with that.

Entry.JapaneseText: 食べるものがなくて、 死んじゃうなんて 今の世じゃ考えられないわね
Entry.EnglishText: It's hard to believe anyone would go without food for so long it kills them, in today's world.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、他の国ではどうあれ、 ヴァルハラでは、 これが現実なのよ……
Entry.EnglishText: But however all those other countries are doing, in Valhalla, this is our reality...

Entry.JapaneseText: おにいちゃん、 とおいところへいったって おばさんがおしえてくれたの
Entry.EnglishText: My big brother's gone somewhere really far away. My aunt told me.

Entry.JapaneseText: おにいちゃん、 いつかえってくるかな？
Entry.EnglishText: But when will my brother come back?

Entry.JapaneseText: おにいちゃんがかえってきたら、 おかあさんもなきやんで くれるのかな？
Entry.EnglishText: Once my brother comes back, will my mom stop crying, too?

Entry.JapaneseText: おにいちゃんがいった とおいところって どこかな？
Entry.EnglishText: Where's the really far away place my brother went to?

Entry.JapaneseText: ぼくもいってみたいな。 おにいちゃんとあいたいよ～
Entry.EnglishText: I want to go there, too. So I can see my brother~

Entry.JapaneseText: おにいちゃんがね、 ちょっとまえからいないの
Entry.EnglishText: My brother hasn't been here for a little while.

Entry.JapaneseText: おほしさまになったんだって おかあさんがいってた
Entry.EnglishText: My mom said he became a twinkly star in the sky.

Entry.JapaneseText: でもおかあさんないてるんだ、 なんでだろう？
Entry.EnglishText: But why is Mom always crying?

Entry.JapaneseText: おほしさまになれると なんかいいことあるのかな？
Entry.EnglishText: Is there something good about becoming a twinkly star?

Entry.JapaneseText: ぼくもおほしさまになりたいな。 あ、でもそうしたら、 おかあさん、もっとなくかな……
Entry.EnglishText: I want to be a twinkly star, too. Oh, but if I did that, my mom would cry more...

Entry.JapaneseText: おにいちゃん、しんじゃったって おじさんがおしえてくれたよ
Entry.EnglishText: My uncle told me my big brother died.

Entry.JapaneseText: しんじゃったってことは もう２どとあえないんだって。 だからおかあさんないてるんだね
Entry.EnglishText: And that when someone's died, you can't see them again. That's why Mom is crying.

Entry.JapaneseText: でもぼくなかないよ。 だってぼくがないたら、 おかあさんなけなくなるもん
Entry.EnglishText: But I'm not going to cry. Because if I cried, my mom wouldn't be able to cry anymore.

Entry.JapaneseText: もうおにいちゃんと あえないなんて…… ぼくもなきたい……
Entry.EnglishText: I can't see my brother anymore... I want to cry, too...

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、なかないんだ！ おにいちゃんがぼくは つよい子だっていってたから！
Entry.EnglishText: But, I won't cry! Because my brother told me I'm a strong little guy!

Entry.JapaneseText: うちの息子が病気にかかり 亡くなりました
Entry.EnglishText: My son fell ill and perished.

Entry.JapaneseText: お医者さんに診せるお金もなく、 栄養をつける食べ物もなく……
Entry.EnglishText: I have no money for a doctor, no way to get nutritious food...

Entry.JapaneseText: 弟の方はまだ今は元気でいます。 でもこの子もいつまで、元気で いられるか……
Entry.EnglishText: His younger brother is still healthy. But I'm not sure he'll stay this way for long, either...

Entry.JapaneseText: そう思うと、 悲しくて悲しくて、 涙が……
Entry.EnglishText: When I think about it, I feel so sad, and then tears start to...

Entry.JapaneseText: 死んだ息子のことを思いだすと 涙があふれてきます
Entry.EnglishText: When I think back on my dead son, I can't stop the tears from welling up.

Entry.JapaneseText: 泣いてばかりじゃダメだとは思う のですが、自分の意思では なかなか止まりません
Entry.EnglishText: I know it's not good to cry all the time, but I can't will myself to stop.

Entry.JapaneseText: そろそろ息子の死を 悲しんで泣くのは やめないと……
Entry.EnglishText: I need to stop crying over my son's death, soon...

Entry.JapaneseText: 下の子に心配されちゃうし、 それに私自身が干からびちゃう。 飲む水も満足にないんだから
Entry.EnglishText: My younger child is worried for me, and I'm wasting too much water on my tears. We don't have much to drink.

Entry.JapaneseText: 泣き疲れて涙が涸れたという話を よく聞きますが、あれって 嘘ですよね
Entry.EnglishText: I've heard of people getting so exhausted from crying that their tears dry up, but those must have been fibs.

Entry.JapaneseText: いまだ、私の涙は尽きません。 息子を失うということはそれくらい 悲しいことなのです。
Entry.EnglishText: I still have plenty of tears left. That's just how sorrowful it is to lose your own son.

Entry.JapaneseText: たった１１歳で死んでしまった うちの息子……
Entry.EnglishText: My son died when he was just 11 years old...

Entry.JapaneseText: 彼の大人になった時の姿を 想像しただけで、また悲しく なってきてしまうのです……
Entry.EnglishText: When I imagine how he might have looked once he grew up, all that sorrow comes flooding back...

Entry.JapaneseText: 残りの水はごく少ない…… 雨が降ればなんとかなるけど その雨も降らないよ
Entry.EnglishText: We have scant little water left... If rain were to fall, we'd manage somehow, but there's no rain, either.

Entry.JapaneseText: このままじゃこの村全体、 ミイラになっちゃうよ
Entry.EnglishText: At this rate, everyone in the village will dry out, like mummies.

Entry.JapaneseText: もっと深く井戸を掘ればヴァルハラの恵みを 得られるはずなの
Entry.EnglishText: If we can dig this well even deeper, we should receive the blessing of Valhalla.

Entry.JapaneseText: 平原の地下深くに潤沢な 地下水脈が走ってるって話だから
Entry.EnglishText: Since they say there's an underground river flowing, deep beneath these plains.

Entry.JapaneseText: とうとう、井戸の水が涸れたよ…… 明日から飲む水、どうすれば いいのかね……
Entry.EnglishText: And now the well's dried up... How are we going to get water to drink tomorrow?

Entry.JapaneseText: 自分のツバでも飲んで 我慢するしかないのかね……
Entry.EnglishText: Maybe we'll just have to make do with drinking our own spit...

Entry.JapaneseText: 私たちが明日生き残るかどうかは 天の気紛れ次第って なんか劇的だね……
Entry.EnglishText: Whether I'll survive tomorrow is all up to the whims of fate... It's like something out of a play, don't you think?

Entry.JapaneseText: ……笑えないけど
Entry.EnglishText: ...It's none too amusing to me, though.

Entry.JapaneseText: 奇跡、なのかね 井戸の水が少し復活したよ
Entry.EnglishText: It's a miracle, I suppose. A little more water's appeared in the bottom of the well.

Entry.JapaneseText: これで少しは私たちの喉を 潤すことはできるわ
Entry.EnglishText: With this, we'll be able to quench our thirst a little.

Entry.JapaneseText: 井戸の底から少し水が湧いて、 私たちの命は筋１本でつながった。 奇跡と言うには程遠いけどね
Entry.EnglishText: Now that a little water's bubbled up at the bottom of the well, our lives are dangling by a single thread. Not much of a miracle.

Entry.JapaneseText: だってこんなわずかな水で この村全部が救われるわけじゃ ないんだから
Entry.EnglishText: After all, it's not like such a tiny bit of water can save the whole village.

Entry.JapaneseText: 守らなくてはいけない法律がない ということは一見 自由にも見えるかもしれない
Entry.EnglishText: If you look at it one way, I guess having no laws you need to uphold could seem like a kind of freedom.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、この村のように法律が ないということは、守ってくれる ものもないということなのだ
Entry.EnglishText: But when you have no legal authority, the way we don't in this village, that means there's no one to protect you, either.

Entry.JapaneseText: 守ってくれるものがないせいで 我らは死にいこうとしている
Entry.EnglishText: Since we have no one to protect us, we're all on our way to our graves.

Entry.JapaneseText: ただ食べるものがない、飲む水が ないというだけの理由で……
Entry.EnglishText: And it all comes down to not having any food to eat, or any water to drink.

Entry.JapaneseText: 例え明日、村の近くで 大きな金鉱が見つかったとしても それが何だと言うんだ
Entry.EnglishText: And even if a huge vein of gold was found near here tomorrow, what would that matter to us?

Entry.JapaneseText: そんなもので我々のここで受けた 惨めな日々がすべてなしに なるわけではないのだ
Entry.EnglishText: It's not like it'd erase all the days of misery we've lived through.

Entry.JapaneseText: どんな幸福も 私という人間の心の欠けた部分を 埋めてくれることはない
Entry.EnglishText: There's a part of my heart what's missing, and no stroke of fortune can ever fill that hole.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私が万が一、明日裕福になっても、 すぐに幸福になれるわけではない。 貧困とはそういうものだ
Entry.EnglishText: If I woke up tomorrow and, against all odds, struck it rich, it still wouldn't make me happy. That's what poverty really is.

Entry.JapaneseText: この村に住む者は みんな互いに迫害された 過去を持って生きている
Entry.EnglishText: Everyone who lives in this village shares in a history of persecution. And now we all live here.

Entry.JapaneseText: だから、その悲しみ、苦しみを わかっている。だからこそ、 お互いを受け容れあうのだ
Entry.EnglishText: Every one of us understands that pain and that sorrow. It's for that very reason that we support each other.

Entry.JapaneseText: ……傷の舐め合いだと 笑うなら笑うがいい
Entry.EnglishText: Maybe you think we're just licking each other's wounds. Well, laugh all you like.

Entry.JapaneseText: だが、我らは互いに 傷つけあうことを好まない、 優しく相手を受け入れ合うのだ
Entry.EnglishText: But we don't find much fun in hurting each other, and so we accept each other, and treat each other with compassion.

Entry.JapaneseText: ここヴァルハラ村は、 戦争で街を追い出された人、 差別された人が集う村だ
Entry.EnglishText: This place, Valhalla, is a village where people displaced by war and victims of discrimination gather.

Entry.JapaneseText: 特別、見て面白いものはない。 興味本位の訪問客はお断りだ
Entry.EnglishText: There's nothing especially interesting to see here. If you're just a curious tourist, you're not welcome.

Entry.JapaneseText: この村の場所は１年前、 ダオス率いる魔物軍と ミッドガルズが戦った戦場跡だ
Entry.EnglishText: One year ago, this village was a battlefield. An army of monster, led by Dhaos, and the Kingdom of Midgard, waged battle here.

Entry.JapaneseText: と言っても特別な何かが あるわけではない
Entry.EnglishText: But even so, there's nothing much to see.

Entry.JapaneseText: 時々、戦争で使われた矢じりや 剣の破片が落ちているのが 見つかるくらいか
Entry.EnglishText: Once in a while, we find something like an arrowhead or a fragment of broken sword fallen on the ground.

Entry.JapaneseText: ここヴァルハラ村に集った 人たちは何も持たずに この街へやって来た
Entry.EnglishText: The people gathered here, in Valhalla, all came with nothing but the shirts on their backs.

Entry.JapaneseText: おまけにここヴァルハラ平原は 貧しく痩せた土地で作物すら 植えても満足に育たない
Entry.EnglishText: And on top of everything, the soil here's not fertile, so crops don't grow too well, either.

Entry.JapaneseText: 近くの地下から採掘される石炭が 村の収入源になっているが、 大した金にもならない
Entry.EnglishText: The village's main source of income is the coal that's dug up nearby, but that money doesn't amount to much, either.

Entry.JapaneseText: それでも我々はこの村以外では 暮らしていけないのだ
Entry.EnglishText: Even so, there's nowhere else for us to live.

Entry.JapaneseText: この村の人々は貧しい。 そして、心も荒んでいる
Entry.EnglishText: The people here are poor. And so, our hearts are hard.

Entry.JapaneseText: しかし、その内面はとても 澄んでいて、とても温かい
Entry.EnglishText: However, underneath it all, there's a certain serenity, and incredible warmth.

Entry.JapaneseText: この村はヴァルハラ、 北の荒れ野に咲く サボテンの花のような村だ
Entry.EnglishText: This village is Valhalla. It's a place like a cactus's flower, blooming in a desolate northern wasteland.

Entry.JapaneseText: トゲだらけで、色気もないが、 打たれ強く、生き永らえる
Entry.EnglishText: It's covered in thorns and there's no charm to it at all, but no matter how much of a beating it takes, it lives on.

Entry.JapaneseText: その花が荒れ野を旅する者の 心をほっと癒してくれる、 そんな場所だ
Entry.EnglishText: And it's a flower that soothes the hearts of any travelers who cross that wasteland. It's that kind of place.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私はね、美人すぎるって 村を追い出されちゃったの。 要するに嫉妬ね
Entry.EnglishText: Me? Oh, they said I was just too beautiful, and ran me out of the village for it. In short, they envied me.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、なんかこの村の人たち、 色々、理由が重いのよね～
Entry.EnglishText: But you know, everyone in this village has a different story, and each one is pretty depressing, really.

Entry.JapaneseText: そう言えば、エルフに生まれたのに 魔法を使えないからって、エルフの 里を追い出された人もいるんだってね
Entry.EnglishText: Actually, I've heard there's someone who was born an elf, but couldn't use magic, so the elves ran him out of their village.

Entry.JapaneseText: なかなかツライわよね～
Entry.EnglishText: Awfully harsh, isn't it~

Entry.JapaneseText: バジルさんって、美形よね～ 惚れるわ～
Entry.EnglishText: But that Basil's such a cutie~ I might be in love~

Entry.JapaneseText: 私の美貌と つりあう感じで いいと思わない？
Entry.EnglishText: He can even measure up my good looks. We'd make a great couple, don't you think?

Entry.JapaneseText: そう言えば、エルフって みんな美形なのよね～ もしかして私もエルフなのかしら？
Entry.EnglishText: Actually, all the elves are beautiful, aren't they~ Oooh, maybe I'm actually an elf?

Entry.JapaneseText: そう言えば、みにくいアヒルの群れに 白鳥が混じってると迫害されるって 聞いたことあるし……
Entry.EnglishText: Actually, I've heard that if there's a single beautiful swan living with a group of ugly ducks, the ducks will oppress it, so...

Entry.JapaneseText: 私が美人すぎて、 村を追い出されたのも…… ……なんて冗談冗談
Entry.EnglishText: Me being too beautiful, and being chased out of my village over it... Ahaha, I'm joking, I'm joking.

Entry.JapaneseText: バジルさんって 好きな人いるのかしら？ どんな趣味なのかしら？
Entry.EnglishText: I wonder if Basil has someone he likes...? Does he have a type?

Entry.JapaneseText: ねぇ、あなたたち、 ちょっと聞いてきてくれない？
Entry.EnglishText: Hey, won't you go ask him for me? Please?

Entry.JapaneseText: 村は貧しくても 恋する心は捨てちゃ いけないと思うの
Entry.EnglishText: I don't think anyone should give up on love just because they live in a poor village.

Entry.JapaneseText: バジルさんに捧げる恋心、 いつまでも秘めてなんて おけないわ……！
Entry.EnglishText: I can't keep my feelings for Basil secret forever...!

Entry.JapaneseText: お金はなくても、 愛さえあれば！
Entry.EnglishText: Even if you have no money, as long as you have love!

Entry.JapaneseText: 支えあう人と人！ 響き合う笑い声と笑い声！ さぁ、前向きに前向きに！
Entry.EnglishText: Two people, supporting each other! Their two laughs, echoing together! Okay, now, let's think positive!

Entry.JapaneseText: つらいことも悲しいことも 楽しい気分でいれば、 全部、吹き飛ばせるわ
Entry.EnglishText: The painful things, the sad things... As long as you hold happiness in your heart, they'll all fly away.

Entry.JapaneseText: 明日はなんとかなるなる、 そう考えていれば 今日がんばることができるの
Entry.EnglishText: Tomorrow will work out, somehow or other. As long as you keep thinking that way, you can do your best today.

Entry.JapaneseText: 悲しいと思うから悲しい、 つらいと思うからつらい、 要は気分しだいよね
Entry.EnglishText: If you think something's sad, you'll feel sad. If you think it's painful, it'll hurt. It's all about how you feel.

Entry.JapaneseText: 幸せだと思えば、 幸せなのよ、毎日が
Entry.EnglishText: If you believe you're happy, then you'll feel happy, every single day.

Entry.JapaneseText: 食べるものもない、 病気になっても薬も買えない、 それは確かよ
Entry.EnglishText: I don't have any food, and if I fall ill, I won't be able to buy any medicine, certainly.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、空気はキレイだし おなかが空くのも度を越せば 頭も冴えてくるものよ！
Entry.EnglishText: But, the air's so crisp and refreshing! And if you're hungry enough for long enough, it helps clear your mind!

Entry.JapaneseText: そう思うと なんかいい感じじゃない？
Entry.EnglishText: When you think of it that way, don't you feel pretty good?

Entry.JapaneseText: ダメだわ…… 村の中にネガティブな空気が 広がってる……
Entry.EnglishText: This isn't good... There's a negative vibe spreading throughout the village...

Entry.JapaneseText: “絶望”は、どんな病よりも 厄介なものなのよ。 人を死に至らしめるの
Entry.EnglishText: "Despair" is more dangerous than any disease. It leads people to their demise.

Entry.JapaneseText: どんなイヤなことがあっても ほら前向きに、前向きに！
Entry.EnglishText: Whatever awful things happen, you just have to think positive!

Entry.JapaneseText: 気休めだとしても、前向きに 考えることが、私たちの生活 そのものを変えてくれるわ
Entry.EnglishText: It may just be placebo, but thinking positive can still change our very lives.

Entry.JapaneseText: シグルドの連中に追い出されて ここ１か月あまり、平原の中で 野宿状態さ
Entry.EnglishText: I was chased out of town by those Sigurd guys, and spent a month and change camping out in the fields.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、街も解法されて ようやく仕事に戻れる。 「紅の月」の採掘にな
Entry.EnglishText: But now the town's been liberated, and I can finally get back to work. My work? Mining "Crimson Moon."

Entry.JapaneseText: 野宿は意外と楽しかったな。 ウサギを追ったり、 食える野草採ったりな……
Entry.EnglishText: Camping was more fun than I would've thought. Chasing rabbits, gathering wild vegetables...

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、吹きっさらしだし、 寒いんだ。 やっぱり村の中が最高だ
Entry.EnglishText: But there's not a windbreak in sight, so it's always cold. Turns out living in a village really is just better.

Entry.JapaneseText: 「紅の月」の鉱山も シグルドの連中に押さえられてて 採掘もできなかったんだ
Entry.EnglishText: The "Crimson Moon" mine shafts were all sealed off by Sigurd, too, so we couldn't even mine.

Entry.JapaneseText: その間の分、取り返すために 一生懸命働いてるよ
Entry.EnglishText: I'll have to give it 110% if I'm going to make up for all that lost time.

Entry.JapaneseText: １日辺りに掘り進むノルマが １人に課せられてるんだ
Entry.EnglishText: Each miner has a minimum digging quota for the day.

Entry.JapaneseText: ついでに「紅の月」を見つけたら ボーナスありだからね、 否が応でも仕事に力が入るさ
Entry.EnglishText: If you find "Crimson Moon" along the way, you get a bonus. Like it or not, you'll put your back into the work, sure as anything.

Entry.JapaneseText: 明日の仕事のために、 今日はゆっくり休むぞぉ
Entry.EnglishText: I'm taking a nice rest for today, so I'll be ready to work hard tomorrow.

Entry.JapaneseText: ……とその前に…… 休憩前の一杯をやらなきゃな……
Entry.EnglishText: ...But before that... I think I'll grab myself a drink...

Entry.JapaneseText: 仕事を毎日がんばれるのも １日の最後にやる一杯が 楽しみだからだよな～
Entry.EnglishText: What's my motivation at work? Knowing that at the end of my shift, there's a cold pint waiting for me~

Entry.JapaneseText: な、きみもそう思うよな…… ……って、子どもにゃ わからんか……
Entry.EnglishText: Hey, you feel me, right? ...Wait, you're just kids... Never mind.

Entry.JapaneseText: なんでもこの村にさ、 すごい儲け話があるって 言うじゃない？
Entry.EnglishText: So, like, I heard you can make a totally crazy amount of money in this village, you know?

Entry.JapaneseText: わざわざ砂漠越えて来たってのに なんか戦争してるしさ、 本当困った困った……
Entry.EnglishText: So I came aaaall the way through the desert, and then they were having some kind of war? It was sooo stressful...

Entry.JapaneseText: くんくん…… うーん、金の匂いとか しなそうな村ねぇ……
Entry.EnglishText: *sniff* *sniff* Hmm, this village doesn't really have the *smell* of money...

Entry.JapaneseText: 本当にこんな村に 儲け話なんて 転がってんのかしらね
Entry.EnglishText: Is there reaaally any way money's going to just, like, fall into my lap? *Here*?

Entry.JapaneseText: この村の近くじゃ、 「紅の月」っていう稀少金属の 原石が採れるって言うじゃない
Entry.EnglishText: So, like, don't they say you can find ore with that super rare "Crimson Moon" stuff, like, pretty close to here?

Entry.JapaneseText: 金儲けの種って これだったのねぇ
Entry.EnglishText: So thaaat's how those people make their money.

Entry.JapaneseText: ルミネイト約１グラムで 3000ガルドが相場だって いうから、事と次第によっては……
Entry.EnglishText: The going price for about one gram of Luminate is, wow, 3000 Gald! Or so I hear? So that means, if I were to...

Entry.JapaneseText: ふっふっふっふ…… 問題は「紅の月」のルミネイトの 含有量よねぇ……
Entry.EnglishText: Heh heh heh heh... So the only question is, how much Luminate, "Crimson Moon," does this ore actually contain...?

Entry.JapaneseText: 「紅の月」で金儲けをするため、 この村に来たのよ
Entry.EnglishText: I came here to make money dealing in "Crimson Moon."

Entry.JapaneseText: まずは協力してくれそうな採掘者を探さないとね
Entry.EnglishText: So, first, I just need to find some nice, *pliable* miners to help me out.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私が「紅の月」掘り出すのに 手を汚すわけには いかないじゃない？
Entry.EnglishText: I mean, there's, like, no way I'd actually do the mining myself, you know? "Crimson Moon" or not, mining's just too dirty.

Entry.JapaneseText: ここでひとやま大儲けすれば 生涯の後の半分は遊んで 暮らせるわね
Entry.EnglishText: I just need to amass a *smaaaall* fortune here, and then I can spend the whole rest of my life living it up!

Entry.JapaneseText: 絶対、「紅の月」の原石、 がっぽりいただいて帰るわよ？
Entry.EnglishText: I'm going to take, like, *soooo* much "Crimson Moon" ore with me when I go! Just watch!

Entry.JapaneseText: ここにはもともと住んでた ヴァルハラの住民たちは いないのじゃ
Entry.EnglishText: None of the original residents of Valhalla live here anymore.

Entry.JapaneseText: みんなここへやって来た 採掘者たちに追い出されてしまった
Entry.EnglishText: Everyone was run out of town by the miners.

Entry.JapaneseText: 気の毒にのう……ここの住民たちは 一体、みんなどこへ 行ってしまったのじゃろう
Entry.EnglishText: It's just too cruel... Where have all those villagers even gone?

Entry.JapaneseText: ワシのような年寄りも 小さな子どももおったのに、みんな、 追い出されてしもうたのじゃ
Entry.EnglishText: There were old codgers, like myself, as well as tiny little children, and they were all run out, just the same.

Entry.JapaneseText: ヴァルハラの住民と採掘者の争いは 最初は些細なことだったのじゃ。 生活のマナーとかそういうな
Entry.EnglishText: The conflict between the villagers and the miners was small, at first. Always over little things, like people not minding their manners.

Entry.JapaneseText: 小さなことが少しずつ重なり、 大きくなっていて、やがて 取り返しがつかなくなったのじゃ
Entry.EnglishText: But add one little thing on top of another and, soon enough, it was just too much. They couldn't see eye to eye any longer.

Entry.JapaneseText: 最初、住民たちの方が、 採掘者を追い出しに かかったのじゃ
Entry.EnglishText: The residents tried to chase the miners out of town first.

Entry.JapaneseText: じゃが圧倒的に採掘者の方が 力が強くて、逆に住民たちの方が 追い出されてしもうたのじゃ
Entry.EnglishText: But the miners were far stronger than they were, so they didn't stand a chance. Before long, it was the residents who'd been run out.

Entry.JapaneseText: 先に手を上げた方が悪いと 採掘者連中は言うかもしれんが……
Entry.EnglishText: The miners might say, "Well, they started it, so it's their own fault," but...

Entry.JapaneseText: 住民たちを追い出した採掘者が 今度はシグルドに 村を追い出されおった
Entry.EnglishText: The miners ran the villagers out of town, and then got chased out, themselves, by Sigurd.

Entry.JapaneseText: 自業自得だと思っとったが 再び村は採掘者の天下じゃ
Entry.EnglishText: I was thinking "you reap what you sow," at first, but now the miners are back again, and they've claimed the whole village.

Entry.JapaneseText: ワシはただの旅人、 首をつっこむつもりはないが……
Entry.EnglishText: I'm just a traveler, so I'll be keeping my nose out of all this, but...

Entry.JapaneseText: いろいろと腑に落ちんのじゃ。 だからと言うて、何をするという つもりもないのじゃが……
Entry.EnglishText: Something about this situation is just so bitter, I can't seem to swallow it. Still, it's not for me to meddle.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私はシグルドに捕まってたのですわ ああ、本当にこわかったですわ
Entry.EnglishText: I was captured by Sigurd. It was terrifying, truly.

Entry.JapaneseText: 捕まった他の若い人たちは…… ああ、思い出すのもおぞましい！！
Entry.EnglishText: A lot of the young ones they captured were... Oh my, it's too awful to even think about!

Entry.JapaneseText: 私は年寄りであるせいか 妙に手厚く遇されましたわ
Entry.EnglishText: Perhaps it's because of my age, but they were far more cordial with me.

Entry.JapaneseText: ですが、私以外の捕まった、 特に採掘者はどこかへ連れてかれて そのまま帰ってきませんでしたわ
Entry.EnglishText: But everyone else they captured, particularly the miners, were led off somewhere and simply never returned.

Entry.JapaneseText: ああ、今でもシグルドに捕まってた あの時のことを夜の夢で見ますのよ
Entry.EnglishText: Oh my... I still dream about the time I spent held captive by Sigurd, you know.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私は特別、何をされたというわけ ではないのですけれど…… 血の匂い、血の、匂いが……！
Entry.EnglishText: They didn't do much of anything to me, of course, but... I can still smell the blood... All that blood...!

Entry.JapaneseText: 屈強の人たちが集う中に ひとりだけとても上品な 顔だちの人がいましたですの
Entry.EnglishText: They were a group of brawny ruffians, mostly, but there was one man of exceptional beauty among them.

Entry.JapaneseText: あの人がシグルドのリーダー らしかったですけれど、あんな 冷酷な顔の人……初めて見ましたわ
Entry.EnglishText: He seemed to be Sigurd's leader, but the way he looked, so callous and cold... I've never seen anyone make such a face.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私、シグルドに 捕まっていましたのです
Entry.EnglishText: I was captured by Sigurd.

Entry.JapaneseText: とてもこわかったですけれど、 一生であんな体験、もう２度と できないと思いますわ
Entry.EnglishText: It was absolutely terrifying, but in my whole life, I'll probably never have another experience quite like it.

Entry.JapaneseText: どんな経験もしておくに 越したことはないですわ
Entry.EnglishText: And it's worth experiencing everything in life, at least once.

Entry.JapaneseText: 惜しむべきはもっと冷静で いられたら、って思うことですわ。 せっかくの貴重な体験でしたのに
Entry.EnglishText: My only regret is that I didn't remain a little more composed. It was such a rare and valuable experience, after all...

Entry.JapaneseText: ヴァルハラだ！ ここは ヴァル・ハラなんだ！
Entry.EnglishText: It's Valhalla! This. Is. Val! Halla!

Entry.JapaneseText: ヴァル・ハラ、ヴァ・ル・ハ・ラ！ キャハハハハハ！
Entry.EnglishText: Val! Halla! Va! L! Hal! La! Ahahahahahahahahaha!

Entry.JapaneseText: すげーすげー！ ここってなんかすごい発見が あったんだろ！
Entry.EnglishText: This is awesome! So awesome! They discovered some super cool thing here, didn't they!?

Entry.JapaneseText: すげーすげ！！ す・げ・ぇ……！！ キャハハハハハ！
Entry.EnglishText: Aaaawesome! Awesome! Awe! Some! Ahahahaha!

Entry.JapaneseText: ヴァルハラってなんだっけ！？ アレだっけ！？ アレ！ アレ！？ アレって何だっけ！？
Entry.EnglishText: Valhalla's super cool thing? What was that!? Is it that? That thing! It's that!? Wait, what was that thing!?

Entry.JapaneseText: 忘れちった！ 何だっけ！？ な・ん・だ・っけ？ キャハハハハハ！
Entry.EnglishText: I don't remember! What was it!? What. Was. It!? Ahahahahahahahaha!

Entry.JapaneseText: 紅の月だ！ 思い出した！ 紅の月が採れるんだぜ！ それってどれくらいすげーんだ！？
Entry.EnglishText: Crimson Moon! I remember now! You can find Crimson Moon here! How aaaaawesome is that, huh!?

Entry.JapaneseText: オレ知らね、おまえも……知らね。 キャハハハハ！
Entry.EnglishText: I dunno! And you dunno, either! Ahahahahahahaha!

Entry.JapaneseText: 父ちゃんと一緒に村に来たんだ！ なのに、父ちゃんは迷子だ！ 大人なのに迷子になるなよ！
Entry.EnglishText: I came to this village with my dad! But now I can't find him! Maybe he got kidnapped!? But he's an adult!

Entry.JapaneseText: 大人なのに迷子！ 大人なのに迷子！ キャハハハハ！
Entry.EnglishText: Can adults even be kidnapped!? Adults...kidnapped!? Adults...kidnapped! Ahahahahahahahahahahahahahahaha!

Entry.JapaneseText: この街ってすげーイナカだよな！ でもそこがいいよな！
Entry.EnglishText: This town's totally in the sticks! But that's kind of awesome, too!

Entry.JapaneseText: この暑イナカ、ようこそイナカに…… ……なんてな！ キャハハハハハ！
Entry.EnglishText: It's so hot your clothes'll stick, out here in the sticks! Ahahahahahahahahahahaha!

Entry.JapaneseText: たくさん人がシグルドに 殺されたらしい。 採掘に来ていた私の弟もまた……
Entry.EnglishText: Sigurd killed an awful lot of people, it seems. My younger brother came here to mine, and they killed him, too...

Entry.JapaneseText: 許せない、見境なく 人の命を奪うなど、 ケモノと同じだ！
Entry.EnglishText: It's unforgivable. Killing anyone and everyone, indiscriminately... They're no better than animals!

Entry.JapaneseText: こんな何もない汚い村に 弟は夢を賭けていたのか……
Entry.EnglishText: My brother's dreams were riding on this village, empty and dirty as it is.

Entry.JapaneseText: 絶対一儲けして、大きな家を 両親に建ててやるって…… 嫌な予感が当たってしまった……
Entry.EnglishText: "I promise you, I'll earn some good coin, and then I'll build a big house for Mom and Dad"... I had a bad feeling about it...

Entry.JapaneseText: 私の弟の命を奪った シグルドも、ブレイナーも 許せない……
Entry.EnglishText: I'll never forgive Sigurd or Brynhildr. They took my brother's life.

Entry.JapaneseText: どうすればあいつの魂は 救われるのだろうか……
Entry.EnglishText: What can I do to help put his soul at ease...?

Entry.JapaneseText: 花を供えても お祈りをしても 墓を建てたとしても
Entry.EnglishText: I can leave flowers for him. I can pray for him. I can bury him, and have a nice headstone made for him.

Entry.JapaneseText: この無念の気持ちは 鎮まらない……
Entry.EnglishText: But none of that will ease the grief I carry in my heart.

Entry.JapaneseText: シグルドの残党が まだ各地に残っているらしい
Entry.EnglishText: It seems there's still a lot of Sigurd remnants, all over.

Entry.JapaneseText: 弟を殺したシグルドが憎い…… 復讐のために、私もその残党狩りに 参加することに決めたのだ
Entry.EnglishText: I hate them for killing my brother, so I've decided I'll help root out their remnants. It's my way of taking revenge.

Entry.JapaneseText: シグルドを全滅させるまで 故郷に帰らない決意をした この誓いは絶対なのだ
Entry.EnglishText: I won't return home until every single Sigurd member is dead and buried. I swear to that, here and now.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私はヴァルハラの元住民です。 採掘者の集団に追い出されました が、こっそり戻ってきました
Entry.EnglishText: I'm a former resident of Valhalla. I was chased out by a gang of miners, but I've returned now, and I'm keeping quiet.

Entry.JapaneseText: すっかり村はあの人たちのものに なってしまって…… 私たちは許せません……
Entry.EnglishText: This village belongs to them now, completely and utterly. It's absolutely despicable...

Entry.JapaneseText: 村がシグルドに占領された時は ざまぁみろと思いました
Entry.EnglishText: When Sigurd occupied the village, I thought, "Ha, serves 'em right!"

Entry.JapaneseText: あ、決して私たちがシグルドを 仕掛けたわけじゃありませんよ？
Entry.EnglishText: Oh, but of course I didn't have anything to do with Sigurd coming here.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私が住んでいた家も採掘者のものに なっていました
Entry.EnglishText: The house I lived in also belongs to a miner, now.

Entry.JapaneseText: 「紅の月」なんてものが見つかった せいで私の愛したこの街が 荒らされてしまうなんて……
Entry.EnglishText: The town I loved has been totally ruined, and all because someone discovered that "Crimson Moon"...

Entry.JapaneseText: 村の通りはゴミだらけ、 人と人がケンカしてても みんな見て見ぬふり……
Entry.EnglishText: The main roads are covered in trash, people are fighting each other in the streets...

Entry.JapaneseText: 街のマナーは最悪です。 もうこの街には私たち 元の住民の居場所はありません
Entry.EnglishText: These people have no manners at all, and there's no place here for us former residents. Not anymore.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私たちの先祖は自分たちの村を 追い出され、この村を築きました
Entry.EnglishText: Our ancestors were all chased from their own villages, so they came here, and built this one.

Entry.JapaneseText: その子孫である私たちが再び この村を追い出されようと しています
Entry.EnglishText: And now we, their descendants, have been chased from the village they built, once again.

Entry.JapaneseText: 歴史は繰り返す、 といったところなのでしょうか？
Entry.EnglishText: I suppose this is what they mean when they say "History repeats itself."

Entry.JapaneseText: 私たちは再び安住の地を見つけ そこにまた新たなヴァルハラ村を 作りたいと思います
Entry.EnglishText: We'd like to find a safe and peaceful land, and build a new Valhalla Village there.

Entry.JapaneseText: 次は誰にも見つからない、 静かな場所に……
Entry.EnglishText: But it will have to be somewhere quiet, where no one will ever find us...

Entry.JapaneseText: いやいや、うはうはうは…… まったく笑いが止まらんとは このことだな
Entry.EnglishText: My word, isn't this delightful... This is precisely the sort of thing that would put a smile on anyone's face.

Entry.JapaneseText: 紅の月が予想以上に高く売れて 大金を手にしたんだ
Entry.EnglishText: I can sell Crimson Moon at a far higher price than I had anticipated, and so I've acquired a great deal of money.

Entry.JapaneseText: 大量に採掘者を連れて この村に来てよかったわい
Entry.EnglishText: I brought a whole legion of miners with me when I came to this village, and that was an excellent decision.

Entry.JapaneseText: これでまた事業も拡大できる。 鉱脈が続く限りはしばらく、 この村の世話になるかの
Entry.EnglishText: I should be able to expand my business now. I suppose I'll remain in this village, for so long as this vein of ore allows.

Entry.JapaneseText: もともとこの辺りの鉱脈は ヴァルハラの原住民のもの だったのだ
Entry.EnglishText: Originally, the veins in this region were property of the residents of Valhalla Village.

Entry.JapaneseText: だが、紅の月があるらしいとの 噂を聞きつけて、この村へワシが 乗り込んできたのが３年前
Entry.EnglishText: But I came here three years ago, as soon as I heard the rumors concerning the presence of Crimson Moon.

Entry.JapaneseText: すぐさま掘ってみたら、 これまた出るわ出るわ…… うはうはうはじゃ、うはうは
Entry.EnglishText: We need but to dig straight ahead, and we find ever more ore. More, always more... It's positively delightful.

Entry.JapaneseText: ヴァルハラ住民からは ワシは正当にこの鉱脈の権利を 買い取っておるのだ
Entry.EnglishText: I acquired the legal rights to this vein via purchase from the residents, all above-board.

Entry.JapaneseText: ワシは何も悪いことなど しとらんはずだ。悪人みたいに 言われても困るってもんじゃ
Entry.EnglishText: You'd be hard-pressed to claim I've done anything wrong. It would be most troubling if anyone were to brand me as a villain.

Entry.JapaneseText: シグルドを率いていたブレイナーは この村に住んどったバジル博士 だったらしいじゃないか
Entry.EnglishText: So it seems Brynhildr, who led Sigurd, was in fact the professor, Basil, who once lived in this village.

Entry.JapaneseText: バジル博士は元の住民のために 村を解放しようとしてたって話が 広まり始めておる
Entry.EnglishText: Rumor would have it that the professor was making an effort to liberate the village, for the sake of its former residents.

Entry.JapaneseText: おかげで世間の風当たりがきつい、 ワシの立場が危ういのじゃ……
Entry.EnglishText: As a result, I've been under a great deal of scrutiny, and faced not inconsiderable criticism. My position is not so secure, now...

Entry.JapaneseText: そろそろ、ワシもこの村から 手を引くよい潮時かもしれん
Entry.EnglishText: In which case, the moment may have come for me to take my exit from this village.

Entry.JapaneseText: けっこう儲けさせてもらったし 他の業者の連中もぞろぞろ 来よったしの……
Entry.EnglishText: I've indeed made a great deal of profit here, but there's rather a lot of competition, now, besides...

Entry.JapaneseText: なんかこの村、 不快な空気が漂っているね……
Entry.EnglishText: The vibe of this village is somehow...uncomfy...

Entry.JapaneseText: 君たちは…… おや、君たちはずいぶん キレイな空気の持ち主だね
Entry.EnglishText: And you guys are... Well, I'll be. Your vibes are immaculate, actually.

Entry.JapaneseText: うん、この村は どうも金の亡者の 不快な空気でいっぱいだ
Entry.EnglishText: Yeah, this village has soaked up the uncomfy vibes of a lot of nasty, money-hungry types.

Entry.JapaneseText: ……なーんてね。 でも真面目な話、耳を傾けると 嫌な話ばかり聞こえてくるね
Entry.EnglishText: ...Heh, just yankin' your chain. But no cap, if you listen in a little, you'll hear nothin' but bad things about this place.

Entry.JapaneseText: 以前からこの村は 小さくて貧しい村だった
Entry.EnglishText: This village was small and poor for a long, long time.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、だからって卑屈にならず 諦めや絶望を抱かず強く生きている 人たちばかりが集まっていたんだよ
Entry.EnglishText: But 'cause of that, a lot of fearless, strong, determined, "never say die" types gathered and made their homes here.

Entry.JapaneseText: 以前のこの村は 悲しいながらにもっと 健全で誠実な空気に溢れていた
Entry.EnglishText: There used to be a lot of sorrow in this village, but the vibes were always wholesome and honest, relative to...this.

Entry.JapaneseText: それが今は誰をどう 騙して、どう出し抜こうという 空気でいっぱいなんだ
Entry.EnglishText: And now the vibes are all, "Hey, who am I gonna screw over?" and "Yo, where's the next sucker?"

Entry.JapaneseText: お金があるのはないよりは 確かにマシだね。 でも、マシってだけだ
Entry.EnglishText: I mean, it's certainly "greater" now than it was when no one had any cash. But... "greater" in one sense, and only one.

Entry.JapaneseText: そんなにお金ばかり持って、 みんなどうしようと言うんだろうか
Entry.EnglishText: And what's even the point, if they have nothing but money to carry them through life?

Entry.JapaneseText: 人の貪欲さは無限だ。 だからこそ、最小限で 満足をする必要がある
Entry.EnglishText: The avarice of men knows no bounds. That's why we need to learn to be happy with the bare necessities, and no more.

Entry.JapaneseText: でないと死ぬまで際限なく 何かを求めてしまう
Entry.EnglishText: If we don't, we will spend every day until our very deaths, seeking and craving, without limit.

Entry.JapaneseText: それではいつまで経っても 本当の幸せなんて 訪れないんだよ
Entry.EnglishText: And in that way, we will never know true happiness, however long we should live.

Entry.JapaneseText: まったく部長のヤツ、 こんな汚い村で仕事なんて、 やっぱり左遷じゃねーかよ
Entry.EnglishText: Man, my director's gotta have it out for me, sendin' me out to work in a filthy village like this.

Entry.JapaneseText: しょうがねぇな…… ユークリッドで雇った 採掘者は来てるかなと……
Entry.EnglishText: Well, I'll just have to deal... Hope those miners I hired in Euclid turn up soon...

Entry.JapaneseText: あ、自分はチェン商会の営業マン 商売になる話があるってんで 社命でこんな僻地に転勤だよ
Entry.EnglishText: Ah, I've ended up here on company orders. Merchant group, we'd heard word of some good product opportunities out here, so...

Entry.JapaneseText: こんな支社も何もないところに…… あぁサラリーマンはツライなぁ
Entry.EnglishText: But this branch is out in the middle of nowhere... Damn, I hate bein' a wage slave.

Entry.JapaneseText: 自分はチェン商会の営業マン。 今日も１日フルタイムで勤務中だ
Entry.EnglishText: I'm a businessman, working for a merchant group. I'm on a full shift today—and every day, for that matter.

Entry.JapaneseText: 採掘者のスケジュール管理、 業務指示、日当の支払い、 全部、自分の仕事だ
Entry.EnglishText: Managing the mining shift schedules, directing operations, daily salaries, all of it is my responsibility.

Entry.JapaneseText: 今日もよく働いた。 でもまだ仕事が終らない
Entry.EnglishText: I've worked a lot today. But there's still more to do.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも疲れたから、ひとやすみ。 上司もいないし、自分の管理が できるのは自分しかいないからね
Entry.EnglishText: But I'm tired, so I'm taking a break. My bosses aren't here, so I'm my own manager, really.

Entry.JapaneseText: 紅の月の採掘量が目標数の 半数にも満たない…… このままじゃ、本社に戻れねー！
Entry.EnglishText: This isn't even half the total Crimson Moon we were aiming to mine... No way am I returnin' to HQ like this!

Entry.JapaneseText: 明日から採掘ラインの 稼働時間を２時間延長だ！ 文句は言わさねーぞ……
Entry.EnglishText: A'ight, startin' tomorrow, I'm addin' two hours to every miner's shift! And I'm not takin' any lip, either...

Entry.JapaneseText: ……ラインの稼働時間を 延長したらたぶんすげー 反発されるだろうなぁ……
Entry.EnglishText: ...If I give 'em longer shifts, the blowback's gonna be insane, ain't it...

Entry.JapaneseText: 労働者の権利をどうとか、 ブラックがなんとかって……
Entry.EnglishText: "Who cares if you're in the black? What about our labor rights!?"...

Entry.JapaneseText: ええい、知るか！ 責任は会社がとってくれるわ！
Entry.EnglishText: Man, who gives a shit! The company can deal with all that!

Entry.JapaneseText: 開かないだ。 どうやら留守のようだでな～
Entry.EnglishText: It won't open. Looks like they're not at home.

Entry.JapaneseText: お前が食えったら食え！ この強情っぱりが！！
Entry.EnglishText: If you're gonna eat, then eat! Ya obstinate old crone!

Entry.JapaneseText: あんたが食いなったら食いな！ このトーヘンボク！！
Entry.EnglishText: If you're going to eat, just eat already! You smooth-brained oaf!

Entry.JapaneseText: お兄ちゃん、どの星かな～？？
Entry.EnglishText: Which star is my brother~?

Entry.JapaneseText: はい いいえ
Entry.EnglishText: Yes No

Entry.JapaneseText: 水精石を１０個 渡しただ！
Entry.EnglishText: You handed over 10 Aqua Spirit Gems.

Entry.JapaneseText: ああ、君たちか。 また先生が戻ってきたら、 来てね
Entry.EnglishText: Oh, so it's you guys. Once the professor's returned, do swing by.

Entry.JapaneseText: 先生も君たちに とても会いたがってたから
Entry.EnglishText: He was really hoping to see you again, too.

Entry.JapaneseText: おいおいどこ行くんだべ？ 村の中にいろ言われてんだろ？ これだからボウズは……
バジルっつーのを探すんだべ？ ほったらこの村で探すのが 当然だべ？わからんか、あーん？
バジルから通行証をもらうまで 村から出ねほうがいいぞ？ すぐ迷子になるくせに大人ぶんなや
固く戸締りしてあるだな。 中に人の気配もしないだべよ
